editor: Editors (no named addressee — as original inquiry)
subject: RE: Presubmission inquiry & collaboration — evidence standards for physical-risk disclosure regimes
body:
Dear Editors,

I am following up on my presubmission inquiry of 3 September 2026 regarding a policy analysis, "Disclosure regimes without evidence standards: provenance classes for EU Taxonomy, CSRD and Pillar 3 physical-risk reporting".

The manuscript is now complete: a policy analysis of about 3,600 words, within your Policy Analysis format, with abstract and key policy insights. It compares the three EU regimes textually and proposes a minimal provenance-declaration remedy. Since my first note, the analysis has been extended to the 2025–2026 developments — the Omnibus I scope narrowing, the revised-ESRS package now under scrutiny, and the EBA's June 2026 Pillar 3 ESG proposals — which sharpen, rather than diminish, the case for an evidence standard.

May I ask whether the topic remains of interest to Climate Policy, and whether you have any guidance before submission through the T&F portal? I would be glad to share the abstract, or the full manuscript, if that would help.

Kind regards,
Motaz OMARIEN. Talaix
Earth Observation & Environmental Risk / Financial Decision Intelligence
Luxembourg-based technology team
info@talaix.com | talaix.com
